ux-role.title: O*NET: Web and Digital Interface Designers
ux-role.supports: Interface planning, usability and application models; occupational context, not a universal junior job description.

ux-test.title: GOV.UK: Using moderated usability testing
ux-test.supports: Agree research questions, observe real tasks, and avoid hints in test goals.

ux-observe.title: NN/g: Observer Guidelines for Usability Research
ux-observe.supports: Record participant behavior rather than substituting guesses.

food-role.title: O*NET: Food Science Technicians
food-role.supports: Assist food scientists with standardized tests, sample preparation and records. Used to bound supervised Level 1 work, not to equate all scientist and technician roles.

food-code.title: Iowa State Extension: Sensory Testing in the Winery, Part 2
food-code.supports: Neutral three-digit sample codes and a secure code key reduce expectations. Only this coding method is adapted to the fictional fruit drink, not wine service or tasting instructions.

food-record.title: Penn State Extension: Troubleshooting Milk Flavor Problems for Small Processors
food-record.supports: Consistent sample preparation and records identifying samples. Applied only to record discipline; no dairy safety rule is transferred to this drink.

limits: These sources inform methods and role context. All brands, deadlines, codes and events are fictional. Level 1 is a supervised first week. Changing only fruit amount is this exercise’s assigned comparison, not a universal design-of-experiments rule. No tasting, safety, accessibility or market release is approved by the junior.
